mortgage: Mortgage payments and illustrative PMI are estimates, not a loan offer or approval. Actual escrow costs, insurance pricing, cancellation rights and servicing terms must be confirmed with your lender or servicer.
amortization: The amortization schedule assumes the entered rate and payment timing. Your lender may use different day counts, rounding, fees or payment-crediting rules; use its statements for amounts actually owed.
mortgage-payoff: Projected payoff dates and interest savings depend on extra payments being credited to principal as modeled. Confirm prepayment restrictions, partial-payment handling and a dated payoff quote with your servicer.
house-affordability: An estimated affordable price is not mortgage preapproval or a safe borrowing limit. Underwriting, emergency savings, variable expenses and local ownership costs can materially change your budget.
rent: The modeled rent budget does not establish what you can safely spend or what a landlord will approve. Include utilities, deposits, moving costs and other obligations before signing a lease.
debt-to-income-ratio: The calculated debt-to-income ratio does not determine loan eligibility. Lenders may count income and obligations differently and apply additional credit, reserve and program requirements.
real-estate: These property tools provide planning estimates rather than property valuations, financing commitments or investment recommendations. Verify each linked tool's assumptions and obtain local transaction and lending information before making a decision.
refinance: Estimated refinance savings are not a lender quote. Closing costs, financed fees, a changed repayment term and the time before selling or refinancing again can outweigh a lower monthly payment.
rental-property: Rental returns depend on uncertain occupancy, repairs, financing and resale assumptions. Estimates do not guarantee cash flow or appreciation and do not replace local legal, tax or property due diligence.
apr: This APR estimate depends on which fees and cash flows are entered. Regulatory disclosure rules and lender fee treatment may differ; compare the lender's official Loan Estimate and APR disclosure.
fha-loan: FHA premiums and payments apply only to the stated loan assumptions and rule version. This is not an FHA eligibility or approval determination; confirm loan limits, appraisal, credit requirements and applicable MIP terms with an FHA-approved lender.
va-mortgage: VA funding-fee and payment estimates do not establish entitlement, exemption or loan approval. Verify service eligibility, prior use, exemption documentation and the fee for your actual loan type with the VA and lender.
home-equity-loan: A home equity loan is secured by your property, and failure to repay can lead to foreclosure. The estimate does not determine available equity, approval, closing costs or the lender's actual terms.
heloc: HELOC borrowing is secured by your home. Actual rates, draw restrictions, interest-only rules and repayment resets may change payments substantially; confirm the agreement and your ability to repay.
down-payment: Estimated down payment and cash needed are not a complete closing-cost or cash-to-close quote. Program eligibility, reserves, appraisal differences and mortgage insurance may require additional funds.
rent-vs-buy: The rent-versus-buy comparison is sensitive to uncertain rent growth, maintenance, investment returns and sale costs. It cannot predict market prices or determine the best personal housing decision.
auto-loan: Vehicle financing estimates exclude costs not entered and do not guarantee dealer or lender terms. Confirm taxes, trade-in treatment, fees, insurance requirements and the signed finance agreement.
cash-back-or-low-interest: The better modeled vehicle offer depends on the entered rebate, rates, term and eligibility. Dealer fees, credit qualification, tax treatment and early payoff can change the comparison.
auto-lease: Lease estimates are not a dealer offer. Actual residual values, money factors, acquisition fees, mileage limits, wear charges and early termination terms must be checked in the lease contract.
interest: An assumed interest rate and contribution schedule do not guarantee the projected balance. Actual crediting, rate changes, taxes and account charges can differ from the model.
investment: Projected investment balances are hypothetical and do not guarantee returns or protect principal. Actual volatility, contribution timing, fees and taxes can produce materially different outcomes.
finance: Time-value-of-money results depend on the selected compounding, payment frequency and cash-flow timing. They are mathematical scenarios, not a valuation guarantee or a recommendation to borrow or invest.
compound-interest: Compound-growth projections assume the entered rate and contribution timing. Market returns are not constant, and actual losses, charges, taxes and withdrawals can substantially change the outcome.
interest-rate: A solved rate is the mathematical rate required by the entered cash flows, not an available investment yield or borrowing quote. Verify that compounding and payment timing match the real product.
savings: Savings projections assume the entered deposits, rate and timing. Account rate changes, withdrawal restrictions, taxes and fees can prevent the projected goal from being reached on schedule.
simple-interest: Simple-interest estimates do not establish how a particular contract accrues charges. Verify its day-count basis, dates, payment allocation, fees and whether compounding applies.
cd: CD estimates depend on the entered yield, term, compounding and tax assumptions. Confirm the issuer's disclosure, early-withdrawal penalties, renewal terms and applicable deposit-insurance coverage; coverage is not verified here.
bond: Estimated bond prices and yields depend on the modeled coupon and timing conventions. They do not eliminate default, interest-rate, liquidity or call risk; verify settlement terms and the issuer's documents.
mutual-fund: Fund projections use assumed returns, expenses and contributions. They do not predict performance or guarantee principal; review the prospectus for risks, share-class fees and actual expense treatment.
average-return: Arithmetic, geometric and cash-flow-based returns answer different questions and may differ substantially. Results from entered historical cash flows do not predict future investment performance.
irr: IRR depends on cash-flow timing and can have multiple roots or no meaningful solution. A reported rate alone does not establish investment quality; consider NPV, risk and realistic alternative uses of capital.
roi: ROI reflects only the costs and proceeds entered and may not represent an annualized return. Missing taxes, fees, holding costs or the time value of money can change the economic result.
payback-period: Payback estimates do not by themselves establish profitability. Cash flows after payback, risk, liquidity and the selected discount rate can change whether a project is worthwhile.
present-value: Present value is sensitive to the chosen discount rate and cash-flow timing. It is not a market appraisal or guaranteed transaction price; uncertain cash flows require separate risk assessment.
future-value: Future value assumes the entered rate and payment schedule persist. It is not a forecast of actual market returns, and taxes, costs, inflation and interrupted contributions may reduce the outcome.
retirement: Retirement projections cannot guarantee that savings will last. Longevity, sequence of returns, inflation, healthcare costs and changing tax rules require review alongside your personal circumstances.
401k: 401(k) projections and withdrawal estimates are limited to the stated contribution-year and tax assumptions. Employer plan rules, vesting, eligibility, Roth treatment and actual withdrawal taxes require confirmation with the plan administrator or tax adviser.
pension: Pension comparisons depend on entered benefits, discount rates, life expectancy and survivor terms. They do not determine plan entitlements or guarantee payments; review the plan's official benefit and election documents.
social-security: Social Security estimates do not retrieve your earnings record or establish eligibility. Actual benefits depend on SSA records, claiming rules and personal circumstances; confirm estimates with your official SSA statement before claiming.
annuity: Annuity values are mathematical estimates, not insurer quotes or guarantees of insurer solvency. Actual fees, surrender charges, riders, tax treatment and contract crediting rules may differ.
annuity-payout: Modeled annuity payouts do not establish an insurer's lifetime-income offer. Mortality assumptions, survivor choices, guarantees, fees and insurer financial strength affect actual payments.
roth-ira: Roth IRA projections do not establish contribution eligibility or tax-free withdrawal eligibility. Verify income limits, holding-period rules, conversion treatment and distribution ordering for your circumstances and tax year.
ira: IRA estimates are not a determination of deductibility, eligibility or distribution taxes. Income limits, workplace-plan coverage, other accounts and applicable tax-year rules require separate verification.
rmd: This RMD estimate covers only the stated owner-account and life-table assumptions. Inherited accounts, exceptions, deadlines and aggregation rules can differ; confirm the required distribution with your custodian or tax adviser.
income-tax: Federal income-tax estimates are limited to the selected tax year and supported items, not a complete return or an IRS determination. Other income, deductions, credits, elections and state or local taxes can materially change liability.
salary: Salary conversions assume the entered working hours, paid time and frequency. They do not determine take-home pay, overtime eligibility, employee status or legal wage entitlements.
marriage-tax: The modeled marriage tax difference covers only the stated federal filing assumptions. Credits, deduction restrictions, state taxes and household-specific circumstances may change the result; filing decisions need individual review.
estate-tax: The federal estate-tax estimate is not an estate valuation, legal plan or filing determination. Prior gifts, deductions, portability elections and state estate or inheritance taxes require qualified review.
take-home-paycheck: Take-home pay is an estimate under the stated federal year and entered withholding assumptions. State and local rates are inputs rather than complete jurisdictional tax models; actual payroll deductions and final annual tax can differ.
loan: Loan payments and interest are estimates, not approval or an offer of credit. Actual APR, fees, compounding, payment dates and prepayment provisions must be checked against the lender's contract.
payment: A solved payment or loan amount assumes the entered rate, term and timing. It does not determine affordability or credit eligibility; confirm the complete repayment obligation and fees with the lender.
currency: Currency conversion uses the entered manual rate or a disclosed dated snapshot, not an executable live quote. Banks and payment providers may apply spreads, fees and different settlement rates.
inflation: Inflation adjustments use the selected historical data or entered assumptions. They do not predict future inflation or represent every household's purchasing-power change.
sales-tax: Sales-tax amounts depend on the entered rate and price basis. Actual U.S. state and local liability may depend on sourcing, product taxability, exemptions and rounding; confirm the applicable rules for the transaction.
credit-card: Credit-card payoff estimates assume the stated APR, minimum-payment rules and future charges. Daily accrual, changing rates, fees and payment allocation can make issuer statements differ.
credit-cards-payoff: A multi-card repayment comparison assumes the entered balances, rates and payment allocation. Promotional expirations, late fees, new spending and issuer-specific minimums can change payoff dates and savings.
debt-payoff: Snowball and avalanche projections assume the planned payments are affordable and made on time. Rate changes, creditor rules, new charges and fees can change results; these estimates do not resolve legal collection obligations.
debt-consolidation: A lower consolidated payment does not necessarily reduce total cost. Compare the full term, fees, collateral risk and future borrowing; approval and advertised terms are not guaranteed.
repayment: Repayment estimates depend on the entered balance, rate and payment frequency. The creditor's interest accrual, fees and allocation rules may differ; confirm a current statement or payoff quote before acting.
student-loan: Student-loan estimates do not determine federal program eligibility, forgiveness or an income-driven payment. Confirm loan type, capitalization, deferment and repayment terms with the servicer and current program rules.
college-cost: College-cost projections use assumed tuition inflation, aid and investment returns. They do not guarantee admission, financial aid or sufficient savings; compare institution-specific net-price and funding information.
vat: VAT arithmetic does not establish a country's registration, exemption, place-of-supply or filing rules. U.S. sales tax is a different system; verify the applicable jurisdiction, rate and inclusive or exclusive price basis.
depreciation: Calculated book depreciation is not automatically an allowable tax deduction or a market-value estimate. Tax methods, recovery periods, elections and jurisdiction-specific limits require separate verification.
margin: Profit margin, markup and trading margin are different concepts. Stock and foreign-exchange margin estimates do not determine broker requirements or maximum losses; leveraged trading can lead to losses beyond posted funds.
discount: Discount estimates assume the entered price and reduction sequence. Retailer rules, exclusions, tax treatment and additional charges can change the amount payable.
business-loan: Business-loan estimates do not assess approval, operating cash-flow resilience or personal-guarantee exposure. Confirm collateral, fees, covenants, rate changes and default provisions in the financing agreement.
personal-loan: Personal-loan estimates do not guarantee approval or the advertised rate. Origination fees, financed charges, insurance, prepayment terms and credit assessment may change the amount received and total cost.
boat-loan: Boat financing estimates depend on the entered rate, term and purchase costs. Confirm lender fees, collateral requirements, insurance, registration and ongoing ownership costs before borrowing.
lease: Lease-versus-financing estimates depend on entered payments, residual values and fees. They do not determine accounting or tax treatment, and contractual return, purchase and termination conditions can change the comparison.
budget: A budget estimate depends on complete and realistic income and expense entries. It does not guarantee affordability or financial stability; allow for irregular expenses, emergencies and changes in income.
commission: Commission calculations do not establish contractual earnings or employment rights. Actual payouts depend on the agreement, tier definitions, refunds, chargebacks, timing and applicable payroll or tax rules.
percentage: Percentage results depend on the chosen base and operation; a percentage change is different from a percentage-point change. Verify the denominator and rounding before using results in financial or contractual decisions.
tip-bill-split: Tip and split estimates do not determine required gratuities, service charges or local tax treatment. Check the bill and agree on included charges and rounding before settling payment.
date: Date calculations use the selected calendar and inclusion conventions. They do not determine legal, tax or payment deadlines, business-day adjustments or time-zone cutoffs; confirm the governing rule.
unit-converter: Converted values depend on the exact unit definitions and displayed precision. Verify tolerances and independent specifications before using a conversion in engineering, medical or other safety-critical work.
scientific: Scientific results use finite numeric precision and the selected angle mode and expression conventions. Independently verify consequential calculations; this tool is not a certified safety-critical computation system.
markup: Markup is based on cost, while profit margin is based on selling price. Results exclude unentered overhead, taxes, returns and transaction charges and do not guarantee actual business profit.
cagr: CAGR smooths an endpoint change and does not show volatility or intermediate cash flows. It is not a forecast and may not represent an investor's money-weighted or after-tax return.
emergency-fund: An emergency-fund target is a planning assumption rather than a guarantee of adequate protection. Income stability, dependents, insurance deductibles and access to liquid funds can change the amount needed.
break-even: Break-even estimates assume the entered fixed costs, variable costs and selling price remain valid. Capacity limits, demand, taxes, financing and changes in the sales mix can prevent the projected outcome.
investment-fee: Fee comparisons assume the entered returns and expense treatment. Actual returns vary, and product charges, tax effects or already-net performance figures can change the apparent savings; review provider disclosures.
real-return: Inflation- and tax-adjusted returns depend on the selected assumptions and tax timing. They do not predict future purchasing power or account for every investor-specific cost and tax rule.
pmi: PMI estimates are not an insurer quote or a servicer cancellation decision. The dated base-rate card, original-value 80% request, original-schedule 78% and midpoint rules have distinct conditions; verify approval, billing and any investor-specific exceptions with your servicer.
biweekly-mortgage: Biweekly savings assume 26 equally spaced credited payments per year, not an exact dated daily-interest schedule. Servicers may hold partial payments or charge fees; confirm crediting and compare the equal-annual-budget monthly alternative.
discount-points: Discount-point comparisons require actual same-principal, same-term lender quotes. A point does not guarantee a standard rate reduction, and cash-paid fees, sale or refinance timing, taxes and opportunity costs can change whether buying points is worthwhile.
mortgage-recast: Recast results assume a fixed rate, immediate principal reduction and re-amortization over your entered remaining term. Servicer approval, minimum lump sums, fees and processing dates vary. Lower P&I does not reduce taxes or homeowners insurance or automatically remove PMI, and can cost more interest than keeping the current payment. FHA, VA, USDA, ARM and interest-only eligibility are outside this model.
tax-equivalent-yield: Tax-equivalent yield is a conditional comparison, not confirmation of a bond’s exemption or an investment recommendation. Enter non-overlapping effective marginal rates; state/local exemption, AMT, NIIT eligibility, deductions, capital gains, account type, fees and differing credit or duration risks can change actual after-tax outcomes.
treasury-bill: Bill returns assume holding to maturity using your price or bank-discount quote, actual holding days and entered fee/tax rates. Simple annualization is not the Treasury auction Investment Rate, and effective annual yield assumes hypothetical same-rate reinvestment. Live auction pricing, secondary-sale gains, tax-year accrual and broker rounding are not calculated.
roas: Revenue-based ROAS is not profit or a platform bid recommendation. Break-even and target thresholds cover only the entered contribution costs; overhead, tax and attribution differences can change the decision. No ad-account data is fetched.
landed-cost: All shipment costs and import charges are manually entered in USD. This is not a tariff lookup, customs valuation or official accounting calculation. Avoid duplicate bundled fees, distinguish recoverable taxes, and confirm the actual charges and allocation method.
quick-ratio: Accounting quick ratio is a snapshot of entered liquid assets relative to current liabilities, not the SaaS growth metric. Asset quality and payment timing are not assessed. A single ratio cannot establish solvency or a universal healthy threshold.
current-ratio: Current ratio and working capital use the entered current classifications at one date. They are not profitability measures, cash-flow forecasts or lending decisions. Industry context, trends and asset quality matter.
coast-fire: Coast FIRE is an assumed portfolio-growth milestone, not permission to retire or a guarantee of safe withdrawals. You still need to fund living costs before retirement. All amounts are in today’s USD; market volatility, sequence risk, taxes, account access rules and benefits are not simulated.
noi: Property-level NOI before financing, capital expenditure or replacement reserves, depreciation and owner income tax. Enter all money in one selected reporting period; no appraisal or lender-specific underwriting is inferred.
fire: Full FIRE portfolio target and first monthly crossing under constant real-return assumptions. Not Coast FIRE, a retirement drawdown simulation, account eligibility, benefit estimate or probability of success.
mirr: Equal-period signed project cash flows, including time zero. Both rate inputs are effective annual rates converted to the selected spacing; irregular-date XIRR and automatic project costs are excluded.
lean-fire: Budget-based FIRE estimates in today’s USD. Returns are constant assumptions, not forecasts. A withdrawal-rate target does not establish safe withdrawals. Tax allowances are user estimates; benefit timing, account access and tax rules are not modeled.
fat-fire: Budget-based FIRE estimates in today’s USD. Returns are constant assumptions, not forecasts. A withdrawal-rate target does not establish safe withdrawals. Tax allowances are user estimates; benefit timing, account access and tax rules are not modeled.
debt-snowball: Monthly payoff estimate with fixed APRs, fixed entered minimums and no new borrowing or fees. Actual lender interest and payment rules can differ. Cover all minimums before directing extra money; this is not a credit-score, settlement or hardship model.
debt-avalanche: Monthly payoff estimate with fixed APRs, fixed entered minimums and no new borrowing or fees. Actual lender interest and payment rules can differ. Cover all minimums before directing extra money; this is not a credit-score, settlement or hardship model.
hsa: HSA eligibility and tax treatment depend on coverage, other insurance, Medicare and applicable rules. Limits use the selected 2025 or 2026 year. Tax savings use entered marginal rates, not a full tax-return calculation. Growth assumes fixed returns and qualified medical distributions; investments can lose value. The tool does not apply the last-month rule or correct excess contributions.
self-employment-tax: Regular U.S. Schedule SE method for entered net profit and wages, using selected 2025/2026 limits. This is not a complete tax return or required estimated-payment calculation. Special eligibility, optional methods, community-property complications and tax treaties are not modeled; confirm filings using official instructions.
barista-fire: Barista FIRE combines assumed after-tax earnings and portfolio withdrawals. Earnings may end or fall, healthcare costs may change and investments can lose value. This constant-return model funds a dated bridge and checks a full-retirement sizing target; it does not simulate lifetime withdrawals or establish a safe withdrawal rate. Include taxes and insurance in your budget, and separately check access to retirement accounts. No automatic Social Security, pension or insurance benefits are included.
brrrr: BRRRR results use entered property values, rent, expenses and financing assumptions. Refinance availability, appraisal, seasoning and cash-out limits are not established. Cash received from refinancing is borrowed money, not profit. No sale, tax or lender-specific underwriting is calculated. Negative rental cash flow and additional closing cash can occur; a cash-on-cash percentage is not defined when no positive cash remains invested.
cash-on-cash-return: Cash-on-cash return measures one year of cash flow against the stated cash investment. It excludes appreciation, sale proceeds, tax deductions and principal paydown as income. The rental worksheet assumes immediate stabilized operations, unchanged costs and a fixed-rate loan; the headline cash yield deducts a separate capital reserve. A zero or negative cash basis does not define a return percentage. Results are estimates, not investment quality scores or lender approval.
mortgage-vs-invest: The comparison uses a hypothetical constant investment return and a fixed mortgage rate with identical initial cash, monthly budgets and horizons. Investment results are not guaranteed. Mortgage-interest deductions, penalties, taxes on withdrawals, PMI changes and account access are not calculated. Equal monthly growth is a mathematical reference, not a risk-adjusted investment recommendation. Review liquidity needs and actual loan terms.
house-hacking: House hacking estimates use your entered tenant rent, losses, costs and financing assumptions. They do not establish occupancy, zoning, licensing, loan eligibility, mortgage insurance pricing or tax treatment. Your own living space is excluded from rental cash income. Budget differences versus renting are not profit, ROI or a promise of free housing. Annualized values repeat a stabilized month; they are not a forecast of actual yearly costs.
covered-call: Expiry-only illustration for a standard fully covered stock buy-write. No investment advice, live premium pricing, assignment prediction, tax calculation or guaranteed annual income. Stock losses can outweigh premium; gains are capped. Enter a consistent new-trade stock price and fees.
drip: Hypothetical single-asset projection with fractional shares; not investment advice or a stock forecast. Dividends can be cut, prices can fall, and reinvesting does not guarantee a higher ending value. Flat dividend tax only; no sale tax, fees, inflation or tax-lot model.
roth-conversion-ladder: U.S. calendar-year early-bridge illustration for one owner and fully taxable traditional IRA conversions. Flat conversion tax from outside cash; no brackets, pro-rata basis, earnings withdrawals, exceptions, age-59½ transition or eligibility determination. A five-tax-year conversion clock is not qualified-distribution status. Not personalized tax advice.
cap-rate: Cap rate uses your annual NOI and property value. Income-capitalization values are scenarios, not appraisals or investment recommendations. Financing, capital replacements, owner income tax and future sale returns are excluded.
credit-card-minimum-payment: This estimate uses your selected minimum-payment rule and monthly interest. Actual statement minimums, daily accrual, fees, rounding and changing rates may differ. Check your card agreement and statement.
